items.title: Entropic temperature, pressure, and molar chemical potentials
items.statement:
Fix a material constitution $c$, with $r$ named species and dimensionless equilibrium state domain $D_c\subseteq\mathbb R^{r+2}$ from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. For $x=(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)\in D_c$, define the diagonal SI coordinate map

$$\Phi_c(x):=(U_c(x),V_c(x),n_{c,1}(x),\ldots,n_{c,r}(x))=(\hat U\,\mathrm J,\hat V\,\mathrm{m^3},\hat n_1\,\mathrm{mol},\ldots,\hat n_r\,\mathrm{mol}).$$

In SI numerical coordinates this is a diagonal linear bijection with a diagonal linear inverse, so it maps ambient open sets to open sets and its inverse is defined on its image.

Choose an open subset $O\subseteq D_c$ in the ambient dimensionless Euclidean coordinates that is designated as a single-phase chart, and set $\Omega:=\Phi_c(O)$, an open chart of physical SI coordinate values. Here $U$ is the internal-energy coordinate evaluated in the center-of-mass rest frame of [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]]. If $S_c:D_c\to\mathbb R$ is the entropy adopted by [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]], define its physical-coordinate representative on $\Omega$ by

$$S_c^{\mathrm{SI}}:=S_c\circ\Phi_c^{-1}:\Omega\to\mathbb R.$$

When its arguments are the physical coordinates $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, write this representative as $S_c(U,V,n)$ for brevity. On $\Omega$, assume the finite representative is $C^2$ and has $S_{c,U}>0$, as adopted by [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]. Here $C^2$ means that all coordinate partial derivatives through order two exist and are continuous ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). A coordinate partial such as $S_{c,U}$ is the ordinary derivative in the physical $U$ coordinate while every other physical coordinate is held fixed, as in [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]; in particular the conversion factor from $\hat U$ is included.

Explicitly, with the partial derivatives on the right taken in the dimensionless coordinates on $O$ while holding every other hatted coordinate fixed, the physical partials are

$$S_{c,U}^{\mathrm{SI}}=(1\,\mathrm J)^{-1}\partial_{\hat U}S_c,\qquad S_{c,V}^{\mathrm{SI}}=(1\,\mathrm{m^3})^{-1}\partial_{\hat V}S_c,\qquad S_{c,n_j}^{\mathrm{SI}}=(1\,\mathrm{mol})^{-1}\partial_{\hat n_j}S_c,$$

using the coordinate-conversion convention of [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]].

Define the physical-coordinate representatives of the **absolute thermodynamic temperature**, **entropic pressure**, and **molar chemical potential** of species $j$ by

$$T_c^{\mathrm{SI}}:=\frac{1}{S_{c,U}^{\mathrm{SI}}},\qquad p_c^{\mathrm{SI}}:=T_c^{\mathrm{SI}}S_{c,V}^{\mathrm{SI}},\qquad \mu_{c,j}^{\mathrm{SI}}:=-T_c^{\mathrm{SI}}S_{c,n_j}^{\mathrm{SI}}.$$

For a state-domain point $x\in O$, define the corresponding state functions by pullback, $T_c(x):=T_c^{\mathrm{SI}}(\Phi_c(x))$, $p_c(x):=p_c^{\mathrm{SI}}(\Phi_c(x))$, and $\mu_{c,j}(x):=\mu_{c,j}^{\mathrm{SI}}(\Phi_c(x))$. When the argument is a physical tuple $(U,V,n)$, write $T_c(U,V,n)$, $p_c(U,V,n)$, and $\mu_{c,j}(U,V,n)$ for the physical-coordinate representatives. Thus both notations refer to the same state functions through $\Phi_c$.

The entropy unit is $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, the energy $U$ is in joules, $V$ is in cubic metres, and $n_j$ is in moles ([[def-td-si-quantities]]). Thus $S_{c,U}^{\mathrm{SI}}$ has units $\mathrm{K^{-1}}$, $T_c$ is finite and positive in kelvins, $S_{c,V}^{\mathrm{SI}}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$ and $p_c$ has units pascals, and $S_{c,n_j}^{\mathrm{SI}}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$ and $\mu_{c,j}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$. If a microscopic model instead uses a dimensionless particle count $N_j=N_{\!A}n_j$, the corresponding per-particle chemical potential is $\mu_{c,j}/N_{\!A}$ joules, with the exact SI Avogadro constant from [[def-td-si-quantities]].

These are scalar state functions of the stated rest-frame equilibrium chart. The pressure in this definition is a derivative-defined conjugate; identifying it with force per area requires a separate adopted mechanical coupling. Neither an empirical thermometer calibration nor any equation of state is supplied by this definition.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §§1.2.4 and 1.4
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapter 2, §2.9

items.physical_scope: Smooth single-phase charts with positive finite entropy derivative in the adopted nonrelativistic macroscopic thermodynamic framework; the quantities are state functions, not empirical thermometer readings.

items.title: Mechanical pressure-volume work coupling
items.statement:
For a simple-compressible system whose only admitted mechanical equilibrium coordinate is volume, model the piston as a planar boundary of fixed area $A>0$ in $\mathrm{m^2}$ that translates only along its outward unit normal without changing shape. Let $\ell$ in metres be its outward displacement coordinate, so the enclosed volume is $V_*+A\ell$ for a fixed reference value $V_*$. Let $\Omega$ be an open positive-temperature single-phase chart of equilibrium states, with equilibrium states as in [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]].

A **quasistatic piston leg** in this postulate is a map $\theta\mapsto(U(\theta),V(\theta),n,\ell(\theta))$ on a compact interval $J=[\alpha,\beta]\subseteq\mathbb R$, with $\alpha<\beta$, of a dimensionless parameter, fixed composition $n$, $V(\theta)=V_*+A\ell(\theta)$, and the system in an equilibrium state at every $\theta\in J$. Each coordinate function is continuous on $J$, differentiable on $(\alpha,\beta)$, and has a derivative extending continuously to $J$; equivalently the leg is $C^1$ in its Euclidean coordinates. A **piecewise-$C^1$ quasistatic piston path** is a finite concatenation of these legs with matching endpoint state and piston position. The path is **frictionless** when the tangential contact force vanishes on every leg. It is in **mechanical equilibrium** when the net normal force on the piston is zero at every path point; thus the external load balances the system's outward normal force. Write $F_{\mathrm{sys}}(\theta)$ for the signed outward normal force component, measured in newtons, exerted by the system on the piston, and define the oriented mechanical pressure by $p_{\mathrm{mech}}(\theta):=F_{\mathrm{sys}}(\theta)/A$, in pascals.

For every such path, adopt the identification

$$p_{\mathrm{mech}}=p_c,$$

where $p_c$ is the derivative-defined pressure of [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]], evaluated at $(U(\theta),V(\theta),n)$. With $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ positive for work done on the system, the system's outward work on the piston is $F_{\mathrm{sys}}\,d\ell$, so the coupling assigns the work increment along the path

$$\delta W_{\mathrm{on}}=-p_{\mathrm{mech}}A\,d\ell=-p_c\,dV.$$

Here $\delta W_{\mathrm{on}}$ denotes an increment along the stated path; no path-independence is asserted. This is an adopted, regime-limited physical assumption, not a deduction from the entropy derivative or from the first-law balance [[post-td-first-law-energy]]. It makes no claim for friction, paths outside the quasistatic regime, changing piston area, shear, surface forces, fields, composition transfer, or other generalized coordinates.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §1.2.4
David Tong, Statistical Physics, Chapter 4, §4.2 The First Law

items.physical_scope: Smooth positive-temperature single-phase charts for simple-compressible systems coupled to a rigid planar constant-area piston along a C1 path of equilibrium states with zero net normal force and no tangential friction; other work coordinates and paths outside this idealized regime are excluded.

items.title: Local energy representation and thermodynamic conjugates
items.statement:
Let $c$ be a material constitution with $r$ named species, and let $O\subseteq D_c$ be an open dimensionless single-phase subset from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. Its physical SI chart is $\Omega=\Phi_c(O)$ under the diagonal unit map $\Phi_c$ defined in [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. Let $(U_0,V_0,n_{0,1},\ldots,n_{0,r})\in\Omega$, with $U$ in joules, $V>0$ in cubic metres, and each $n_j>0$ in moles ([[def-td-si-quantities]]). On $\Omega$, write $S_c(U,V,n)$ for the physical-coordinate representative $S_c\circ\Phi_c^{-1}$; its physical-coordinate partials include the unit factors as specified in [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]. Assume this representative is $C^2$ and $S_{c,U}(U_0,V_0,n_0)>0$. Then there are open neighborhoods of $(S_c(U_0,V_0,n_0),V_0,n_0)$ and $(U_0,V_0,n_0)$ on which the equation

$$S_c(U,V,n)=s$$

has a unique solution $U=\mathcal U_c(s,V,n)$ of class $C^2$. On this local chart,

$$\mathcal U_{c,s}=T_c,\qquad \mathcal U_{c,V}=-p_c,\qquad \mathcal U_{c,n_j}=\mu_{c,j},$$

with the intensive functions defined by [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. This is a local representation only: it asserts neither global injectivity or domain coverage nor differentiability at a nonsmooth phase boundary.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §§1.2.4 and 1.4
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapter 2, §§2.9–2.10

items.physical_scope: Local single-phase, positive-temperature charts of the adopted macroscopic entropy representation; no global inverse or statement at a phase boundary is asserted.

items.title: Interior exchange conditions from entropy maximization
items.statement:
Consider two independent separated subsystems $A,B$ of fixed material constitutions, with states in domains $D_{c_A},D_{c_B}$ as in [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]], and additive total energy, volume, and aligned mole amounts as in [[post-td-bulk-additivity]] using SI coordinates ([[def-td-si-quantities]]). Let $S_{\mathrm{tot}}=S_A+S_B$ be their adopted total entropy, and let $\mathcal F$ be the exact feasible endpoint set fixed by the totals, retained partitions, and permitted exchanges in [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. Suppose $x_*=(x_A^*,x_B^*)\in\mathcal F$ is a stable equilibrium attaining the global entropy maximum adopted by [[post-td-entropy-maximum]]. Assume both subsystems lie in open $C^2$ single-phase charts with finite positive temperatures, and assume every exchange direction named below is locally feasible for both signs at $x_*$. Then:

- If energy exchange is permitted, $T_A=T_B$.
- If volume exchange is permitted, then $p_A/T_A=p_B/T_B$; if energy exchange is also permitted, this gives $p_A=p_B$.
- If species $j$ can be exchanged, then $\mu_{A,j}/T_A=\mu_{B,j}/T_B$; if energy exchange is also permitted, this gives $\mu_{A,j}=\mu_{B,j}$.

The pressure equality concerns the derivative-defined pressures of [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. It is equality of mechanical piston pressures only when the coupling of [[post-td-mechanical-conjugate-identification]] applies. A retained volume or species constraint supplies no corresponding equality.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §§1.2.4 and 1.4
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapter 2, §2.9.1

items.physical_scope: Attained global equilibrium maxima for two independent separated systems in smooth single-phase positive-temperature charts, with only the specified energy, volume, and species exchanges permitted.

items.title: Concave entropy, constrained maxima, and local stability
items.statement:
Let $C$ be an open convex region of dimensionless numerical coordinates for a compound of independent separated systems, and let $S_{\mathrm{tot}}:C\to\mathbb R$ be the adopted $C^2$ concave total entropy on a smooth single-phase chart. Let the feasible set be the affine slice $F=C\cap\{x:Ax=b\}$ for a fixed real linear map $A$ and vector $b$. For the following conclusions, assume the mathematical input that for differentiable concave $f$ on an open convex $C$, an interior point of $C\cap\{x:Ax=b\}$ whose derivative vanishes on $\ker A$ is a global feasible maximizer; strict concavity gives at most one maximizer; for $C^2$ concave $f$, the Hessian quadratic form is negative semidefinite. Under this input, if $x_*\in F$ is interior relative to this slice and $DS_{\mathrm{tot}}(x_*)$ vanishes on $\ker A$, then $x_*$ is a global entropy maximum on $F$. If $S_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is strictly concave on $F$, that maximum is unique. The Hessian conclusion does not by itself give strict stability.

The mathematical input is supplied by [[lem-tdmath-concave-affine-maximizer-and-hessian]] on the stated region and admissible affine segments.

There is a further conditional scaling conclusion. On a designated open single-phase bulk cone $C_c\subseteq D_c$ with the common constitutive law adopted by [[post-td-common-bulk-constitutive-law]], the $C^2$ entropy Hessian has zero radial direction: $D^2S_c(x)[h,x]=0$ for every $x\in C_c$ and every vector $h$. This branch adopts coordinate-preserving entropy transport between the distinct scaled-system tag and one fixed material-law chart, with common species, units and reference conventions. The null-direction conclusion is not asserted for the general tagged family from [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]] and [[post-td-bulk-additivity]] alone.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §1.4.3
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapter 2, §§2.9.1–2.9.2

items.physical_scope: C2 single-phase entropy charts and explicitly convex affine slices of permitted exchange coordinates; the radial-curvature conclusion applies only to the separately designated common-constitutive-law bulk cone with its adopted entropy transport and common reference conventions.

items.title: Thermodynamic response functions on valid local charts
items.statement:
Fix a constitution $c$ and an open dimensionless subset $O\subseteq D_c$ in the single-phase region of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. Its physical chart is $\Omega=\Phi_c(O)$, where $\Phi_c$ is the SI coordinate map defined in [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. For fixed physical amounts $n=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)$ with nonempty slice $\Omega_n:=\{(U,V):(U,V,n)\in\Omega\}$, this slice is open in $\mathbb R^2$. Use $T,p$ from [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]] as functions of the physical coordinates on $\Omega_n$. For a response derivative, restrict to an open neighborhood in $\Omega_n$ where the required natural-coordinate map is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism onto an open image, so its inverse expresses the physical $(U,V)$ as $C^1$ functions of those natural coordinates ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Specifically, $C_V$ uses $(U,V)\mapsto(T,V)$ at fixed $n$, while $C_p$, $\kappa_T$, and $\alpha_p$ use $(U,V)\mapsto(T,p)$ at fixed $n$. The existence of each such local chart is a hypothesis for its response derivative, not a consequence of this definition. Each derivative uses the indicated natural variables and holds all other listed coordinates fixed.

The **constant-volume heat capacity** and **constant-pressure heat capacity** of the whole system are, where the derivatives exist and are finite,

$$C_V:=\left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial T}\right)_{V,n},\qquad H:=U+pV,\qquad C_p:=\left(\frac{\partial H}{\partial T}\right)_{p,n}.$$

Here $H$ is the enthalpy in joules; both heat capacities are in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, not per mole. The **isothermal compressibility** and **isobaric thermal expansion coefficient** are

$$\kappa_T:=-\frac{1}{V}\left(\frac{\partial V}{\partial p}\right)_{T,n},\qquad \alpha_p:=\frac{1}{V}\left(\frac{\partial V}{\partial T}\right)_{p,n}.$$

Since $V>0$ and the coordinates use SI units ([[def-td-si-quantities]]), $\kappa_T$ has units $\mathrm{Pa^{-1}}$ and $\alpha_p$ has units $\mathrm{K^{-1}}$. This definition asserts no sign for any response, no identity among them, and no finite value at a critical or otherwise singular chart.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §1.2.4
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapter 2, §2.10.5

items.physical_scope: Finite response derivatives on smooth positive-temperature simple-compressible charts at fixed composition; no positivity or finite-response claim is made outside the specified charts.

items.title: Response functions in a formal logarithmic entropy chart
items.statement:
Fix a constitution $c$ and an open dimensionless single-phase subset $O\subseteq D_c$ whose physical chart is $\Omega=\Phi_c(O)$ under [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. Fix positive amounts $n=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)$ for which the slice $\Omega_n:=\{(U,V):(U,V,n)\in\Omega\}$ is nonempty, and assume $\Omega_n\subseteq\{(U,V):U,V>0\}$. Let $a,b>0$ have units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, with reference values $U_0>0$ joules and $V_0>0$ cubic metres. Stipulate the physical-coordinate entropy representative on $\Omega_n$ (denoted by $S_c(U,V,n)$ as in [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]) by

$$S(U,V)=a\ln(U/U_0)+b\ln(V/V_0).$$

Applying the definitions on this chart gives

$$T=U/a,\qquad p=bT/V,\qquad C_V=a,\qquad C_p=a+b,\qquad \kappa_T=1/p,\qquad \alpha_p=1/T.$$

This is a formal chart calculation, not measured data and not a claim that this entropy satisfies the track's tagged bulk-scaling postulate for a fixed material type.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §1.2.4
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapter 2, §2.10.5

items.physical_scope: A constructed fixed-composition smooth chart used only to evaluate the preceding definitions; it is not an empirical equation of state or a complete bulk model.

items.title: Stable equilibrium with retained unequal volumes
items.statement: For each of two separated fixed-composition subsystems $i\in\{A,B\}$, let $O_i\subseteq D_{c_i}$ be an open dimensionless single-phase subset with physical chart $\Omega_i=\Phi_{c_i}(O_i)$ as in [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. Fix positive amounts $n_i$ with nonempty physical slices $\Omega_{i,n_i}:=\{(U_i,V_i):(U_i,V_i,n_i)\in\Omega_i\}$. Fix $U_0>0$ joules and $V_0>0$ cubic metres, and set $V_A=V_0$ and $V_B=2V_0$. Assume $\Omega_{i,n_i}\subseteq(0,2U_0)\times(0,\infty)$ and $(U,V_i)\in\Omega_{i,n_i}$ for every $0<U<2U_0$ and each $i$. Let each physical-coordinate entropy representative be $S_i(U_i,V_i)=a\ln(U_i/U_0)+b\ln(V_i/V_0)$ on its slice, where $a,b>0$ are in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. The isolated compound permits energy exchange but retains the volume and mole partitions, and its adopted total entropy is $S_A+S_B$. For total energy $2U_0$, stipulate that every split $0<U_A<2U_0$, $U_B=2U_0-U_A$ with these retained volumes and amounts is admitted, and that these are exactly the feasible endpoints. As additional model input, designate the split $U_A=U_B=U_0$ as a stable equilibrium. This designation must satisfy [[post-td-entropy-maximum]], which supplies a necessary maximum criterion rather than a converse. The unique entropy-maximizing energy split is $U_A=U_B=U_0$, so $T_A=T_B=U_0/a$, while $p_A=bT_A/V_0$ and $p_B=bT_B/(2V_0)=p_A/2$. Thus this model's stable equilibrium under energy exchange does not imply pressure equality when volume exchange is retained.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §1.2.4
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapter 2, §2.9.1

items.physical_scope: A constructed two-subsystem entropy-maximization example with fixed volumes; it illustrates the effect of retained constraints and is not an empirical model of a named substance.

items.title: Tagged bulk scaling need not be homogeneity within one fixed tag
items.statement: The tagged bulk-scaling relation of [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]] together with the additive coordinate composition of [[post-td-bulk-additivity]] forces the fixed-tag identity $S_c(\lambda x)=\lambda S_c(x)$ for each material constitution $c$.

references.title: Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapter 2, §2.9.2
David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §1.4.3

items.physical_scope: A formal constitutive-data countermodel to a logical implication between the framework's tagged scaling and entropy-additivity postulates; it is not an empirical model of a material.
